chapter: Gulf Coast and later working bands
title: Working for Rene Louapre and business cards, giving up playing
summary: Hirsch recalls booking jobs through Henry, his blank cards, and Rene hiring him; he stopped after eye trouble.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And Henry asked him, he said, what'd you fire me for? He said, we don't need you no more. We're doing business. We don't need a man anymore. Uh-huh. So, they, then he let him go. And, uh, Joe never would have told me that, but, uh, Henry did tell me that, because I was, I worked with Henry after, after I left Pete. And I was with Henry with, who was booking most of the Lou Wopps jobs. And, uh, in fact, we had quite a, with Rene, he didn't want, he didn't want Henry to use me. He said, because Henry, Godfrey's a leader. He says, he'll take the jobs. He, he says, he don't need your jobs. He says, uh, he'll pay you a commission on the jobs that he gets if, if it, if it interferes with you. Which we never did. I never did get around to it. But I never did take any of these jobs. I don't, I don't, there was no job that was worth it to me to, to take it away from anybody. That's when I started making these cards with, with, like, with Henry. I used to give out when, it's, like, Sidney Castane would say, Godfrey, give me one of your cards. I want to get in touch with you. I want to, I want to know how to get your band or something like that. I don't know if there was any here in there. No. It's not here. I think it's somewhere else. But I used to take a blank card on both sides and say, here's my card. I move around so much I don't even have time to put an address on the thing. And that was it. And, uh, that was it until, after a while, I mean, uh, Renee regarded me as a friend and knew that I wasn't out to chisel against him. Now, in fact, I worked with Renee before I gave up playing, I was supposed to work the whole carnival season with him. And then I had trouble with my eye. And I couldn't drive down to the, uh, auditorium. And then, uh, I was having a lot of trouble with my eye. So I just canceled the jobs. And I, uh, and a couple other jobs, you probably were on with me, with Cindy Castane, with things like that. And Renee had a great, like, one job that I played with him out at the Museum of, uh, New Orleans Museum of Arts. Uh, I came out the scene one night after, I think after, after we played Across the Lake. You remember when we played that New Year's Eve? Came over to see, uh, uh, uh, uh, we drove over there after the job. He says, what are you doing next Saturday night? I got a big wedding. I says, I'm doing nothing. He says, you got a job. He says, come on over. He said, be at the Museum of Art. He says, get there for such and such a time. I said, you don't have to hire me. He says, I want you. And then he was that kind of a guy. Uh-huh. You worked with Renee, didn't you? Sure, sure.
He never, he was never cheap about anything.
I can say one thing about Renee. Class act. He was, he was, he was okay. He was funny. He was a funny guy, but you had to know him to understand him. Sure.
He enjoyed being funny. He knew, he knew he was being that way and he, he enjoyed it.
Renee was something. So what else you want to know about me?
